title: Retry failed refunds with backoff
summary: Failed refunds now retry with growing, random waits and stop after 5 attempts. Retries can no longer refund a customer twice.

steps.title: Retries flooded the gateway
steps.body:
Before this change, a failed refund retried every 60 seconds, forever.

During a gateway outage, every failed refund retried at the same moment. The retries kept the gateway down.

steps.title: A retry could refund twice
steps.body:
A retry after a timeout sent the same refund again. When the gateway had already refunded it, the customer got the money twice.

So the fix must spread retries out and make a repeated refund safe.

steps.title: The decision
steps.body:
- Each retry waits a random time under a cap that doubles.
- Retries stop after 5 attempts.
- The refund id goes to the gateway as an idempotency key.
- An error that can never succeed fails the refund at once.

steps.title: Refunds and attempts
steps.say: A refund is the unit of work. Everything else counts or times its attempts.

terms.meaning: Money that goes back to the customer for a payment.
One try to send a refund to the gateway.
A gateway error that can succeed on a later attempt.

steps.title: Waiting and repeating safely
steps.say: Between two attempts the worker waits. A repeated attempt must not refund twice.

terms.meaning: A wait between attempts that grows after each failure.
Randomness in the backoff, so retries do not all start at once.
An id that lets the gateway ignore a refund it already did.

steps.title: The worker counts each attempt
steps.say: The worker now saves the attempt count before it sends the refund.

notes.text: Before, the worker sent the refund without counting.
The count goes up first. If the process crashes during the call, the attempt still counts.

steps.title: Attempts stop at five
steps.say: `retryRefund` checks the limit before it calls the gateway.

notes.text: `MAX_ATTEMPTS` is 5. `BASE_DELAY_MS` is the first wait cap.
A refund at the limit fails with reason `max_attempts`. The gateway gets no call.

steps.title: The refund id is the key
steps.say: The gateway call now carries an idempotency key.

notes.text: Before, a repeated call looked like a new refund.
The refund id is the key. The gateway ignores a refund it already did.

options.why: The count is saved before the call starts.

options.text: It resets to 0 on the next run.

steps.say: A failed attempt either waits for a later run or fails the refund for good.

steps.title: Only retryable errors retry
steps.say: An error that cannot succeed later fails the refund at once.

notes.text: A `GatewayError` with `retryable` false marks the refund failed with its code.

steps.title: Random waits under a doubling cap
steps.say: Each retry waits a random time below a cap that doubles.

notes.text: `nextDelay` doubles the cap per attempt and picks a random wait below it.
The next attempt number sets the cap.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: Why does each retry wait a random time?

options.text: So that retries after an outage do not all hit the gateway at once.
options.why: Jitter spreads the retries over time.

options.text: So that the gateway cannot guess when the next retry comes.
options.why: This is not a security measure.

options.text: To keep the total retry time under 60 seconds.
options.why: The waits grow and can be much longer.

steps.title: A closed card fails at once
steps.say: The gateway says the card is closed. No retry can succeed.

messages.label: markFailed(id, card_closed)

steps.title: What to check
steps.body:
- Is 5 attempts the right limit for all payment methods?
- Does every gateway error set `retryable` correctly?
- The attempt count goes up before the call. Is that the intended order?
